component.name: ArchiveFree
component.summary: Look inside archives before unpacking them

description.p: ArchiveFree opens zip, 7z, rar and tar files in a window so you can see what is inside before anything is written to disk. Browse the folders, check the file sizes, preview a document, and then extract everything — or just the two files you actually wanted.

ul.li: Opens zip, 7z, rar, tar (gz, bz2, xz, zst), iso, cab, deb, rpm and more
Browse the contents as folders, with sizes, types and dates
Extract everything, or only what you select, anywhere you choose
Preview text, code and images without extracting the archive
Asks before overwriting — it never silently replaces your files
Handles password-protected and multi-part archives
Create archives with a password or split into parts
Large archives never freeze the window, and every operation can be cancelled

description.p: No adverts, no telemetry, no accounts and no paid tiers. Free software, for good.

screenshot.caption: Browse an archive's contents before extracting anything
Choose exactly where files go, with no surprises
Preview a file without extracting the archive
Create an archive in a few clicks

description.p: Three bugs found by a user, all of which needed fixing at the root.

ul.li: Dragging files out now offers the file target other file managers negotiate on. The constructor used for it does not exist in PyGObject, and the error was being silently swallowed, so only a raw URI list was ever offered — enough for some file managers, nothing for others

Compressing from the file manager while ArchiveFree was already open failed with "this doesn't look like an archive". The flag was parsed in the launching process while the file list was handled in the running one, so the two never met
Compressing from the file manager now closes when it finishes, instead of leaving a window behind. A window you opened yourself still stays

description.p: Build fix: the list of handled file types no longer requires PyGObject to read, so it can be checked on systems without a desktop installed.
Recognises the containers that are really a ZIP, RAR or 7z wearing a different extension.

ul.li: Comic books (.cbz, .cbr, .cb7), e-books (.epub), Java archives (.jar, .war), Android packages (.apk), Python wheels (.whl), browser extensions (.xpi) and Office or OpenDocument files are named properly instead of all reading "ZIP archive"
Comic books can be opened by double-clicking, since nothing else on a stock desktop claims them. E-books, documents and packages stay with their own applications and appear only under "Open With"

description.p: Archives can now be edited, not only read and created.

ul.li: Add files or folders to an existing zip, 7z or tar archive
Delete entries from one, with the Delete key or the menu
Changes are written to a temporary copy and swapped in only once complete, so a failure or a cancellation leaves the original archive exactly as it was

description.p: Fixes found by testing against genuine archives downloaded from the internet, plus faster compression.

ul.li: A compressed tar whose name doesn't say "tar" — a rootfs saved as .iso, say — is now recognised by looking inside it. It previously appeared as one opaque blob instead of hundreds of files
Debian packages listed nothing at all, because 7-Zip descends into the inner tar and reports that instead

Root filesystem tarballs and container layers extract again. Absolute symlinks like /bin/sh are normal in those and were being refused; writing *through* a symlink is still blocked, which is the attack that actually matters
XZ compression now uses every CPU core: a 124 MB archive went from 141 seconds to 82 on four cores, for identical output

description.p: Fixes drag-to-extract in the Flatpak build.

ul.li: Dragging files out of an archive did nothing in the Flatpak. Files were staged in the runtime directory, which the sandbox remaps — so the file manager received a path that did not exist on the host. They are now staged somewhere both sides resolve identically

description.p: Drag files straight out of an archive, and every format you can open you can now also create.

ul.li: Drag entries from the archive into a file manager or onto the desktop to extract them. This works on Wayland, where every other Linux archive manager's drag-to-extract has been broken for years
Create .gz, .xz, .bz2, .zst and .lz4 single-file archives, plus tar.lz4 and tar.lzma — the dialog previously offered 7 formats while the engine could write 14
Right-click entries appear at the top level in Nautilus, Nemo and Caja instead of being buried in a "Scripts" submenu

Install advice for missing helper programs now matches the distribution — dnf on Fedora, pacman on Arch, zypper on openSUSE — with the correct package name for each. It previously told everyone to run an apt command
The first run offers to add right-click menu entries, naming the file manager it found. Thunar and Nautilus store this per user, so a system package cannot set it up for you

description.p: Fixes the right-click menu on XFCE.

ul.li: Thunar's custom-action file uses a non-standard XML declaration that Python refused to parse, so the right-click entries silently failed to install on XFCE — the desktop where they matter most
Menu entries now name ArchiveFree, so they are distinguishable from the archive plugin's own "Extract Here"
The settings page can see the host's file managers from inside the Flatpak

description.p: Bug fixes found by an expanded test suite.

ul.li: Archives named .tgz, .txz, .tbz2 and .tzst are now recognised as tar archives instead of opening as a single unnamed blob
An empty file is no longer identified as an archive by its name alone
Extraction now defaults to the folder the archive is in, rather than wherever you last extracted something
Browse and extract zip, 7z, rar, tar and single-stream archives
Create zip, 7z and tar archives, optionally with a password or split into parts
One-click, reversible option to become the default archive application
